claims.text: Directly deposited elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding are prone to premature failure because elevated temperature enhances Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
A continuous, conformal 50–100 nm Al2O3 layer can be deposited between the zirconium-alloy substrate and elemental Cr coating.
The Al2O3 interlayer will inhibit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The Al2O3 interlayer will preserve the Cr coating's protective benefits in subcritical water.
The Al2O3 interlayer will preserve the Cr coating's protective benefits in accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
The proposed alumina barrier is amorphous.
The proposed alumina barrier is chemically inert under the relevant conditions.
The Al2O3 interlayer physically separates the Cr coating from the zirconium-alloy substrate.
Physical separation by the alumina interlayer reduces atomic mobility at the Cr–Zr interface.
Al2O3 has sufficiently low diffusivity to function as a Cr–Zr diffusion barrier.
The Al2O3 interlayer prevents direct contact between Cr and Zr atoms even at elevated temperature.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve the integrity of the protective Cr coating.
Normal operation is represented by subcritical water at approximately 300°C and 15–16 MPa for extended durations.
Accident-relevant exposure is represented by steam at temperatures up to approximately 1200°C for minutes to tens of minutes.
At 1200°C in steam, the barrier-modified system should develop significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than the unmodified Cr-coated baseline.
Reduced interdiffusion in high-temperature steam should allow the modified system to maintain coating integrity and oxidation protection.
The Al2O3 layer should remain stable in subcritical water at approximately 300°C.
The Al2O3 interlayer should not degrade the thermal or chemical performance of the coating system under normal operation.
Successful performance depends on the alumina layer remaining intact, defect-free, and stable during the specified water and steam exposures.
The long-term adherence and stability of the thin Al2O3 barrier under repeated thermal cycling and neutron irradiation are uncertain.
